title:
What Is That
In Thine Hand?
paragraphs: Moses had a whole speech prepared about why he wasn't the man for this assignment — not eloquent, not confident, not convinced anyone back in Egypt would listen to him. God skipped past every line of it and asked one question instead: what is that in thine hand? It was a stick. The same stick he'd carried through forty forgettable years of watching someone else's sheep in the wilderness, worth nothing to anyone but him.

But the moment he threw it down in obedience instead of gripping it in fear, it became the rod of God — the very instrument that would humble a nation and part a sea. The staff never changed size, weight, or usefulness. What changed was the hand's willingness to let go of it long enough for heaven to rename it. Whatever is already in your hand right now was never too small for God to use — it was just waiting on obedience, not inventory.
